title.narrative: Emergency Response Stranded Ethiopian Migrants in EHoA
Emergency Response Stranded Ethiopian Migrants in EHoA

description.narrative:
IOM har ansökt om medel från Sida för att genomföra projektet ”Facilitating safe return and reintegration of stranded vulnerable Ethiopian Migrants in the East and Horn of Africa”.
Projektperioden är 1 september 2021–1 september 2022. Projektets ändamål är att bidra till en effektiv migrationshantering i Östra Afrika och på Afrikas horn genom ett säkert återvändande, stödinsatser vid återvändande, och återintegrering av särskilt utsatta etiopiska migranter.
IOM föreslår att stödet skall användas för att stärka organisationens kapacitet att bistå särskilt utsatta etiopiska migranter i Östra Afrika och på Afrikas horn. Insatsen skall genomföras under IOM:s ledning i Djibouti, Etiopien, Somalia, Tanzania och Jemen.
Den totala budgeten för insatsen uppgår till 20 000 000 kronor. Utbetalning av beloppet i sin helhet kommer göras vid undertecknandet av avtalet.

The International Organization for Migration (IOM) has applied to Sida for funds of SEK 20 000 000 to carry out the project” Facilitating safe return and reintegration of stranded vulnerable Ethiopian Migrants in the East and Horn of Africa”. The project will be conducted during a 12-month period, 1 September 2021- 1 September 2022.
The intervention aims to contribute to effective migration management in the East and Horn of Africa through safe and dignified return, post-arrival assistance and reintegration of vulnerable Ethiopian migrants. The interventions will cover Djibouti, Ethiopia, Somalia, the United Republic of Tanzania, and Yemen
The International Organization for Migration (IOM) will be the implementer of the project.

The overall objective of the project is to contribute to effective migration management in the East and Horn of Africa through safe and dignified return, post-arrival assistance and reintegration of vulnerable Ethiopian migrants. This is to be achieved through:
1. The provision of tailored humanitarian assistance and protection services in countries of origin and transit
2. Access to return, post-arrival and reintegration assistance in countries of origin and transit

sector.narrative: Facilitation of orderly, safe, regular and responsible migration and mobility

description.narrative:
Overall the objectives of the program where achieved, and in some cases IOM has exceeded its targeted reach. The following are some of the cumulative progress reported:
Outcome 1: Vulnerabilities of stranded migrants are addressed through tailored humanitarian assistance and protection services in transit and countries of origin
IOM indicates 90% of beneficiaries reported they were satisfied with the assistance provided to them.
-The program has facilitated the data collection and analysis on mobility trends, and has managed to publish 25 reports through the Djibouti Displacement Monitoring Matrix (DTM), and dashboards produced by the IOM Regional Data Hub.
-Total of over 135,582 migrant returnees from KSA were registered by IOM Ethiopia (134,802), and IOM Tanzania (780 migrants)
-Total of 11,103 vulnerable migrants received direct assistance which include access to food, water, and medical care (Djibouti 10,160; Tanzania 780; Yemen 163). This indicates the program has reached an additional 4500 migrants than what was targeted.
Outcome 2: Access to return, post-arrival and reintegration assistance in countries of transit and origin is strengthened for vulnerable migrants, with focus on unaccompanied and separated children
- A total of 442 migrants were assisted with Assisted Voluntary Return (AVR) from Tanzania (279) and Yemen (163). This is lower than the initial targeted AVR support to 800 migrants. IOM indicated in the final meeting that they did not meet the targeted numbers due to the conflicts in Ethiopia, were they had to put the AVR assistance on hold, leading to funds being under spent. However, even when the AVR support put on hold, IOM indicated they did support vulnerable migrants with voluntary humanitarian returns (VHR) from transit countries. VHR is when returns are considered a life-saving measure for migrants who are stranded or in detention.
-The development oriented support of the program is considered important to ensure the sustainable reintegration of returnees into their communities, and prevent the risk of re-emigration. The reintegration support is to allow returnees to reintegrate socially and economically into their communities.The program has assisted 132 returnees with individual reintegration support which exceeds the targeted number of reaching 117 individuals.
- A total number of 5,865 migrants (4,809 male , and 1,031 female) have received post arrival assistance in Ethiopia, this also exceeds the 3,100 targeted reach through the program.
